The built-in entity kinds, claim kinds, claim evaluation methods and projections are fixed per build. A specification can add entity kinds, properties of any kind, categories, relationship kinds and verification methods (carried out outside Exegra) through its vocabulary, but it cannot add an evaluation method that Exegra itself runs.

tasks.detail: Known unknown of Claim method registry.
tasks.title: The registry declares methods but the evaluator implements them separately; adding an entry without code leaves the claim not evaluated.
The whole text is re-parsed on every commit and on every source-editor analysis; there is no incremental parsing and no measurement of its cost on large specifications.
The schema.version error message tells the user to run an `exegra migrate` command that does not exist.

tasks.detail: Known unknown of Normal form and hash.
tasks.title: The hash is not cryptographic (cyrb53); it identifies revisions and detects change, it does not resist collisions.
History, undo and redo stacks are unbounded in memory and are not persisted: undo is lost on reload and per CLI invocation.

Only operation transactions and replacement sources are validated before they commit. Undo and redo restore text that was committed before and do not validate again, and reload commits any text that parses, so the model after a reload can carry validation errors.
The session never passes expectRevision or expectHash; only the CLI uses the optimistic checks (--expect-hash).
Behavioral results hold for the listed scenario traces only; there is no exhaustive state-space exploration and no probabilistic evaluation.

Claim evaluation runs on the caller's thread. In the application session.evaluate runs it on the main thread inside every semantic commit, and trace and metric claims run engine scenarios there (src/core/claims.js), unlike the Simulation tab, which runs its scenario in the engine worker. The cost on large models is not measured (WG-4775, finding F06).

Format 2 (integer time units, instances, routes, resources and resource faults, workloads, links, timers, request classes and seeded randomness) runs in the Rust engine; crash-instance, meters and the cost metric do not yet (planned: WG-4741).

One configuration copy per step dominates the cost of large format-2 runs (about 10 to 40 us per step); the queueing fixtures (about 7 and 15 minutes) are gated by EXEGRA_FIXTURES=1 (planned: WG-4741).
Behaviors are flat: a component cannot yet be simulated at a chosen depth, as its abstract behavior or as its children (planned: WG-4666).
The cost of projection on large models has no recorded measurement; the benchmark specification exists for that purpose but no result is recorded.
The references projection draws nothing but a note until an entity is selected, unless the view filters to entity kinds.
Pins are absolute positions; nothing re-anchors them when the model changes.
The score weights are fixed constants chosen by hand; no recorded measurement shows that the lowest score is the most readable layout. Crossings are counted on at most 400 sampled edges.
Automatic layout computes all four methods on every recompute; its cost on large scenes has no recorded measurement.

The layout method chosen for a view is stored only in the browser's localStorage under the project and view: it is not in the specification or the layout file, is not shared and is lost when storage is cleared.
The session writes the current text, not one write per revision; the edit-flow machines in this file abstract that.
Claim re-evaluation and re-projection run synchronously inside every commit with no measurement of their cost on large models.

Import writes the project's files through the persistence service without passing the transaction system, a validation gate or a base-hash check (analyzeSpec is run on the bundle first, but only syntax errors stop it); the session then opens whatever was written, with its validation errors.
Rows beyond the 200-row window of a list can only be reached by narrowing the filter; there is no paging.
src/ui/property-controls.js and src/ui/dialogs.js import each other.
src/ui/dialogs.js and src/ui/property-controls.js import each other.
It is a plain textarea: no syntax highlighting, completion or incremental analysis; the whole draft is analyzed on every pause.
It shows recorded results loaded with the project and cannot execute tests; execution happens only through `exegra verify`.
Rows beyond the 200-row window can only be reached by filtering; there is no paging.
It cannot run the traceability check; without a recorded result it says the check has not been run.
No retry, queue or offline buffer: a failed request is reported once to the caller.
Protection rests on loopback host, loopback origin and a custom header only; any local process can read and write projects while the development server runs.
On Windows the atomic rename is retried and then replaced by an in-place write, which is not atomic.
Import and recording of results write without a base-hash check, and import writes its files one after another, not as one atomic unit.
The journal is read in full on every write to number its next line and is never truncated.

Four paths change project files without a transaction or a journal line (WG-4775, finding F05): the bundle import (tools/workspace.js importProject, scenario import-bundle), tools/import-markdown.js (scenario markdown-import), tools/make-benchmark.js (specs/benchmark/spec.jsonc), and exegra apply when its layout write conflicts after the specification was written (scenario cli-apply-partial-write: the spec write has its journal line, but the transaction's two files are no longer written together). The first three write directly with node:fs or atomicWrite.

Engine input and trace format 2 (contracts engine-input-v2 and trace-v2) are derived by simulationInput whenever a specification uses a format-2 construct (needsFormat2, simulationInputV2 in src/core/sim-input.js) and run by the engine's version-2 semantics (engine/exegra-engine/src/lib.rs dispatches on the version). Not yet: format-2 goldens (tests/conformance/goldens holds version 1 only), and the WG-4741 items: crash-instance, meters and the cost metric in the engine, and calibration, sensitivity, the operating envelope and revision binding of metric claims. A specification that uses no format-2 construct still derives version 1, unchanged.
The engine input (format version 1) carries no bound of a scenario's fault model, so every subset of the scenario's faults is explored; the concurrency bounds of fault models are not applied yet.
A fault acts for the whole run or not at all: a fault without an occurrence cannot act on some deliveries of its event and not on others.
Breadth-first order makes a counterexample one of the fewest steps, but that is not proved.
The Rust explorer for large state spaces is not built yet (planned: WG-4650); it will be checked differentially against this one.
Evaluation errors and failed steps end a path without being reported as such: a configuration whose invariant cannot be evaluated counts as a violation, and a failed step has no successor.

Format 2 inputs are not explored yet (planned: WG-4664, WG-4715). The specified relation adds internal entries to the simultaneous-order choice, the new fault kinds to the mask, and one successor per choice value and per instance of an any route; sampled draws are fixed by a seed named first in the result, and a result is shown as verified only when the scenario has no sampled site. Scenarios with workloads need a short horizon and maxArrivals, and keyed populations of thousands of clients are beyond reach. When a timed fault acts is not explored (WG-4704).
Temporal claims are checked without the claim's negatives and without the trace check's vacuity rules (a never whose matcher cannot occur in the scenario holds here without a note).
A violating prefix of a never or precedes claim is reported as the counterexample, not extended to a complete run; any extension violates it too, but that is not a theorem.

Format 2 is defined in formal/Exegra/Format2.lean for the constructs built so far (instances, routes, resources and resource faults, windows, workloads, links, timers, request lifecycle and measured outputs); formal/Exegra/Resource.lean proves the held-units and queue-bound invariants of a settled resource, the strict FIFO queue of a collapse included. Not defined yet: crash-instance with incarnations, meters and cost (planned: WG-4741).

lift_agrees is stated in formal/Exegra/Lift.lean with its proof left as sorry (pinned on sorryAx); it is checked differentially by tools/differential.js --lift on every liftable golden and generated input (planned: WG-4664).
The determinism property over seeds is not stated as a theorem for format 2 yet (planned: WG-4741).

Results are established by native_decide, so each theorem depends on an auxiliary axiom that trusts the Lean compiler and runtime. Kernel reduction (decide) is not feasible: the expression language's number literals go through Float.scaleB and the visited set hashes strings with String.hash, both opaque to the kernel.
The unbounded proof of an invariant (by induction over the step relation, with the explorer supplying counterexamples to induction) is not built yet (planned: WG-4686).
Claim results are reported by exegra prove only; evaluate and verify do not show them yet.
Negatives of a claim are not explored in Lean: prove checks that a claim holds on every configuration of its scenarios, not that its negatives violate it (WG-4711).
Object and generic types (for example {text, hash} or Operation[]) are opaque to the type check: their values are accepted unchecked.
A response is paired with its request by one correlation field or by count; there is no timeout or ordering rule for unanswered requests at the end of a run.
A field counts as a name when its type text contains the word name or handle; there is no type system for field types, so a party field typed as an opaque string passes rule party-by-id (WG-4697).
Retention is free text: nothing checks that a record's retention and its copies' erasure points agree, and a copy of a copy cannot be declared, since of names records only (WG-4697).

Built (WG-4664, WG-4729) in the Lean semantics and the Rust engine, resource faults included (set-capacity, set-class-limit, collapse-classes, scale-demand, replace-demand; untimed, or windowed through fault-edge steps), and derived from a specification's resources by simulationInput. crash-instance with incarnations is refused by both engines, and the grantable-units check is not repeated after the untimed fault mask (planned: WG-4741).
Processor sharing is not part of format 2; CPU is a FCFS multi-server station (planned: WG-4719).
Credit-based backpressure between components is not represented (planned: WG-4722); autoscaling and cold start are not represented (planned: WG-4720).

Built (WG-4715, WG-4729): open, closed and population workloads, address groups, links (bandwidth, ordering, queue bounds, fan-out, latency) and timers in both engines, derived from a specification's workloads and links by simulationInput (src/core/sim-input.js).
Packet-level networking and packet-rate floods are not represented: a link is a FIFO byte pipe with a latency distribution, one step per message (aggregated mode planned: WG-4718).
Matchmaking gather is writable only as a hand-written behavior (primitive planned: WG-4721).

Built (WG-4715, WG-4729): resource metrics; request classes with the request lifecycle, response time, outcomes, throughput, legitimate refusals (false positives) and transition firings, over the window and per series bucket, in both engines. Not built: link and cost metrics, waiting time per class, resource signals per bucket, time-to-first and time-to-recover, meters, and truncation by an open measured request (planned: WG-4741). Warm-up is declared, not detected.

Built (WG-4715, WG-4729): the metric-bound method is registered and evaluated on format-2 scenarios derived from a specification, reporting model-holds, violated or inconclusive with N, the passes, the fraction and the confidence, with negatives and control negatives. Not built: calibration, sensitivity, the operating envelope and revision binding (asOf is only recorded) (planned: WG-4741).

The status model-holds is implemented: it is a ClaimResult status of src/core/claims.js and the verdict of src/core/metric-stats.js, and metric-bound claims report it. Its final name and display follow WG-4703.

Not implemented (WG-4775, layer 2): no code records real traffic today. The client keeps no log (src/persist/client.js request()), the endpoint logs only an internal error to the Vite logger, and the contract events of this specification occur only in simulated traces.
